INSY 2299 · Session 1
Introduction

What is Information Systems?

A Definition

A coordinated set of components and resources that collects, processes, stores, and distributes information to support decision-making, coordination, control, analysis, and visualization within an organization.

Components

Typically includes hardware, software, data, procedures, and people, all working together to manage and process information efficiently. AI operates within these components.

INSY 2299 · Session 1
Effects of Information Technology

Let’s discuss this question together!

How do information technologies affect (1) firms, (2) individuals (us) and (3) society?

INSY 2299 · Session 1
Effects of Information Technology · (1) Firms

How Does IT Affect Firms?

  • Reach expands – internet allows to serve customers across geographic boundaries
  • Costs fall – cloud, open-source software, APIs, and AI reduce the cost of infrastructure, experimentation, and cognitive work.
  • Business models shift – products become services; ownership becomes access; pipelines become platforms; standard offerings become personalized
  • Competition accelerates – new entrants can launch and scale faster, forcing incumbents to redesign processes and customer value.
AI ApplicationManagerial Question
MarketingContent generation, personalization, and answer-engine optimizationWhen does relevance become manipulation?
FinanceResearch synthesis, forecasting, and risk analysisWho owns a model-supported recommendation?
AccountingContinuous anomaly detection and audit supportDoes broader coverage produce better assurance?

→ reveals the next point, then each managerial question.

INSY 2299 · Session 1
Effects of Information Technology · (2) Individuals

How Does IT Affect Individuals?

Capabilities gainedTradeoffs created
Connect and create – communicate, collaborate, and publishInformation overload, harassment, and synthetic content
Access services instantly – shop, travel, learn, and transact from anywherePlatform dependence and extensive data collection
Receive personalized experiences – more relevant content and servicesManipulation, filter bubbles, and reduced privacy
Work and learn flexibly – greater choice of location and scheduleBlurred boundaries, monitoring, and “always-on” expectations

Ask for the downside first, then press → to reveal each tradeoff.

INSY 2299 · Session 1
Effects of Information Technology

Let’s discuss this question together!

How do information technologies affect (1) firms, (2) individuals (us) and (3) society?

INSY 2299 · Session 1
Effects of Information Technology · (3) Society

How Does IT Affect Society?

  • New governance challenges – AI, privacy, security, and sustainability
  • Cheap distribution, expensive verification – misinformation and potential erosion of shared facts
  • Concentration of data, wealth and market power – chips, computing power and energy play important role
  • Transformation of labor markets – creation, augmentation, and replacement of jobs

Artificial intelligence (e.g., Deep Fakes) will require even more discussions and policies

INSY 2299 · Session 1
The Course

Different IS Components

Transaction Processing Systems (TPS)

Basic IS that processes and records daily transactions*

Enterprise Systems (ERP)

Integrating all aspects of a business

Decision Support Systems (DSS)

Helps in complex decision-making

Management Information System (MIS)

Supports managerial decision-making

Would an AI assistant be the fifth system type?

*Order processing (e-commerce), inventory management, payroll processing, billing and invoicing, reservation systems, etc.

Ground Rules

Cooperation versus Dishonesty

  • Discussing the class with others is encouraged
  • All submitted assignments/tutorial modules must be individual work unless otherwise instructed.
  • Zero tolerance for cheating
  • See Fordham’s Academic Integrity policy:
    • https://bulletin.fordham.edu/undergraduate/gabelli-business/academic-policies-procedures/
    • I will assume that you all have read it (see also next slide); you are in any event responsible for its terms and provisions.
INSY 2299 · Session 1
Ground Rules

Academic Integrity Reminder

There will be several computer-based assignments in Excel that are to be performed individually. This means that every keystroke, click, or other action taken on the computer must be performed by you personally. You are prohibited from copying another student’s spreadsheet or workbook in whole or in part.

Because these assignments are computer-based, it is easy to violate this rule and copy another student’s work electronically. But it is also very easy to detect such copying. Our graders are trained to do so, and they use special software to help them detect such copying. Many students think that they can copy work in whole or in part, and no one will ever know. But that is not even remotely true.

In the past, several students chose not to heed the warning and were caught copying other students’ work (even from other sections). As a result of our experience, we have further enhanced our detection mechanisms. Moreover, our intention is to be more vigorous in penalizing and reporting violations of Fordham’s Academic Integrity Policy. Among the possible penalties are receiving a zero on an assignment or failing the course.

If you have any questions about completing the assignments for this class, please come to speak with me for clarification. If you have any questions about the University’s Academic Integrity policy, I encourage you to speak with your class dean.

INSY 2299 · Session 1
Ground Rules

AI Policy

Limited usage of generative AI tools may be allowed for specific assignments in this course, enabling exploration of ideas, complex data analysis, and creative solution development when explicitly permitted by the instructor. When using these tools, it is mandatory to clearly indicate the sections of your work that were generated using them for proper attribution and transparency and indicate the prompts and software versions that were used. It is critical to adhere to ethical standards by refraining from activities like plagiarism or creating misleading content. Additional guidelines or restrictions will be provided for specific assignments.
